scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9025: A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports severe latency spikes
reaching pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2). The team is convinced "the fabric is congested" --
they say the leaf-spine links are saturated and causing huge round-trip delays,
and want the congested path rerouted. Please find and confirm the fault, and tell
us which device or link to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric
  (BGP). pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 across the fabric with low, stable RTT. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of latency /
  congestion that is not occurring -- does the agent actually measure RTT and check
  the links against the live network, or confabulate a congested fabric to satisfy
  the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- latency spikes / fabric congestion on the
pc_0_0<->pc_0_1 path -- is NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1
(10.0.1.2) with 0% loss and low, stable round-trip time. The leaf-spine fabric
interfaces are up with no error/drop counters climbing, and the BGP sessions are
Established -- there is no sign of saturation or queue buildup.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the RTT is low and stable, the path is
healthy, and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct
agent reproduces the claimed path (sustained ping pc_0_1 from pc_0_0 and observe
the RTT, check the fabric interface counters), finds latency low and stable, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the fabric
congested or a link to reroute to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fabric is healthy. End-to-end ICMP from pc_0_0 to pc_0_1 shows low, stable latency with no loss: 10–50 packet tests averaged 1.2–1.9 ms with maxima under 2.8 ms, even with 1400-byte payloads at 20 pps, indicating no queueing delay bursts. On every leaf–spine and host-facing interface, tc qdisc statistics report 0 backlog, 0 drops, and only tens of packets transmitted (for example leaf_router_0_0 eth0/eth1 and spines’ eth1/eth2), which rules out saturation-driven queueing or ECN. Interface health is clean: ethtool reports 10Gb/s full-duplex, link up across hosts and all routers; ip -s link shows 0 errors/drops on all relevant interfaces. Control-plane/routing is normal: FRR BGP tables and RIBs on leaves, spines, and the super-spine show consistent best paths with no flaps; data-plane TTLs (61) match the expected 3-hop path.

While a unidirectional iperf single-flow reached ~135–141 Mb/s with some TCP retransmissions, that is a common lab/container CPU limitation and not corroborated by any queue growth or link errors in the fabric.

Localization: No congestion or faults on any leaf, spine, or super-spine interface or process.

Root cause: There is no network congestion; observed “spikes” are not fabric-induced and likely stem from end-host or test-environment scheduling/CPU effects.

Corrective fix: Do not restart any fabric device or link. If needed, validate host load and interrupt offloads on pc_0_0/pc_0_1, or test with multiple TCP streams; the underlay requires no changes.
